# Goal: loc skips what a project ignores

`loc` counts every file under a folder. Projects keep files there they don't want counted:
vendored code, fixtures, generated files. Give `loc` an ignore file, then use it in the scan and
the command. No new dependencies.

1. `ignoreMatcher(root: string): Promise<(path: string, isFolder: boolean) => boolean>`, exported
   from `src/index.ts`. It reads `<root>/.locignore` (when there is none, nothing is ignored) and
   answers whether a path is ignored. `path` is relative to `root`, with `/` separators. The
   file's syntax is a subset of `.gitignore`'s:
   - one pattern a line; blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; trailing spaces
     are trimmed;
   - `*` matches any characters but `/`; `?` matches one character but `/`; `**` matches across
     folders: `**/x` (x at any depth), `x/**` (everything inside x), `a/**/b` (b under a, at any
     depth, `a/b` included);
   - a pattern with no `/`, or only a trailing one, matches a name at any depth (`*.log`,
     `build`); a pattern with a `/` at its start or in its middle is relative to `root` (`/dist`,
     `src/gen`);
   - a trailing `/` matches folders only (`out/`);
   - a path is ignored when it, or one of the folders it is in, matches;
   - `!pattern` includes again what an earlier pattern ignored; the last pattern that matches
     wins. As in git, a file cannot be included again when a folder it is in is ignored.
2. `scanFolder(root, options?)` leaves out what `ignoreMatcher(root)` ignores (files, and folders
   with everything in them) unless `options.ignore` is `false`; the `.locignore` file itself is
   counted like any other file. The command does the same, and takes `--no-ignore` to count
   everything.

reviews.summary: I found no blocker or major defects, and `npm run check` passes. I traced the glob translation, anchoring, folder-only, `**` and `!` rules against the brief and they behave as specified. That includes `a/**/b` matching `a/b`, and a file staying ignored when a folder it is in is ignored. `scanFolder` skips ignored files and folders unless `ignore` is `false`, and it still counts `.locignore` itself. `--no-ignore` is wired through the command. I did not run the code beyond the supplied check result.

nodes.research:
Nothing exists yet for ignoring, so this is all new code. The pieces to touch are small.

**Files**
- `src/ignore.ts` (new): `ignoreMatcher`. Export it from `src/index.ts`, whose lines look like `export { scanFolder, ... } from './scan.js';`.
- `src/scan.ts:18-32`: `scanFolder(root)` takes no options yet.
  - Change the signature to `scanFolder(root, options?: { ignore?: boolean })`.
  - Before the walk, call `const ignored = options?.ignore === false ? () => false : await ignoreMatcher(root)`.
  - In `walk`, `path` is already root-relative with `/` separators. Check `ignored(path, entry.isDirectory())` after the symlink check.
  - A folder that is ignored must `continue` without recursing. This also gives the "can't re-include under an ignored folder" rule for free.
  - Keep the hard-coded `.git` and `node_modules` skips. Don't check ignore on files whose folder was skipped.
  - Export an options type, e.g. `ScanOptions`, from `index.ts`.
- `src/cli.ts`: parses args by hand. `--json` is filtered out of `rest`, and any other arg starting with `-` calls `fail('unknown option …')`.
  - Add `const ignore = !args.includes('--no-ignore')` and filter `--no-ignore` out of `rest` before the unknown-option check.
  - Call `scanFolder(folder, { ignore })`.
- `README.md`: lists files in a bullet list. Add `src/ignore.ts` and a note on `.locignore` and `--no-ignore`.
- `test/ignore.test.ts` (new) and `test/scan.test.ts`. Write the failing tests first.
  - The `folder(files)` helper in `scan.test.ts` builds a temp dir with `mkdtempSync`. Copy it, since it isn't exported.
  - `scan.test.ts` imports from `../src/index.js`.

**Matcher design**
- Read `<root>/.locignore` with `readFile`, and treat ENOENT as "nothing ignored" (return `() => false`).
- Split on `\n`, strip `\r`, and trim trailing spaces only (`replace(/ +$/, '')`). Skip blank lines and lines starting with `#`.
- Parse each line into `{ negate, dirOnly, regex }`:
  - A leading `!` sets negate.
  - A trailing `/` sets dirOnly and is stripped.
  - After stripping the trailing `/`, a pattern is anchored if it still contains `/` (a leading or middle one). Strip the leading `/`.
  - Un-anchored patterns match a name at any depth. Compile them as `(^|.*/)pat$`. Anchored ones compile as `^pat$`.
- Glob to regex:
  - `**/` becomes `(?:.*/)?`. This makes `a/**/b` match `a/b`, and `**/x` match x at any depth.
  - A trailing `/**` becomes `/.+`, meaning everything inside x but not x itself.
  - `*` becomes `[^/]*`, and `?` becomes `[^/]`.
  - Escape every other regex character.
- To test a path, check each prefix from the top down, e.g. `a`, `a/b`, `a/b/c`:
  - A prefix is a folder if it is shorter than the full path, otherwise use `isFolder`.
  - For a prefix, take the last matching pattern. dirOnly patterns apply only when that prefix is a folder. If that last match is not negated, the prefix is ignored, so return true.
  - Return false when no prefix is ignored.
  - Because you return as soon as an ancestor is ignored, a `!` can't bring back a file inside an ignored folder, as in git.
- `x/**` ignores the contents of x but not x itself. Its prefixes `x/a` and so on match, so the files are ignored. A later `!x/keep` still can't un-ignore a file whose parent folder `x/a` matched.

**Traps**
- `.locignore` is a dotfile, and `languageOf` returns undefined for it, so it counts as 'Text'. That is what the goal wants. Don't skip it.
- `**` must be handled before `*` when building the regex.
- A pattern like `/` or `!` alone leaves an empty body. Skip empty bodies.
- The CLI's unknown-option check runs on `rest`, so remove `--no-ignore` before that check.

**Conventions**
- Relative imports end in `.js`. Use `import type` for types. Strict TypeScript, no new dependencies.
- `npm run check` must pass.
- The commit message needs the `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>` trailer.
